attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. He cites the 2020 essay he co-wrote, and the 'still true' judgment is his.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the four areas and the 'even if' qualifier. 'Trouble' is unquantified, but the claim is stated firmly as present fact.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: documented failures or fragility on new or perturbed tasks in each area, in 2024 up to the post. Reading psychological reasoning as theory of mind is reasonable.

evidence.note: GSM-Symbolic, v1 Oct 2024: state-of-the-art open and closed models are fragile on perturbed grade-school math. The abstract shown is from a later revision, but the 2024 date holds.
Oct 2024 preprint: state-of-the-art LLMs rely on shallow heuristics in causal reasoning. The wording read is from a 2025 revision.
Oct 2024: multimodal LLMs did worse than children on embodied physical common-sense tasks.
Oct 2024: limited theory-of-mind ability on varied tasks. Only open-source models were tested, so it is weaker for the frontier.
OpenAI's own disclosure of o1's AIME gains. It is not a perturbation or held-out robustness test, so it does not show that the trouble was gone.
Peer-reviewed, May 2024: GPT-4 at or near human level on several theory-of-mind tests, though it struggled with faux pas. Partly cuts against the psychological strand.

reviews.rationale: 2024 studies document fragility or failure on new or perturbed tasks in all four areas (e1–e4). The counterevidence is limited: e5 is a company benchmark claim with no robustness test, and e6 shows strong but incomplete theory-of-mind results, with struggles on faux pas. That falls short of the contract's bar of reliable human-level performance on perturbed tasks, so the support condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, stating his view in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful paraphrase. But who made the 'initial promises', when, and what 'remotely' means are all unspecified.

contract.note: The contract is cautious and does not stretch either way. But Marcus supplied no baseline of promises or measure of shortfall, and the contract itself admits that picking one would decide the verdict.

evidence.note: The ChatGPT launch post (2022) admits factual errors. It could be a baseline, but Marcus never names it.
Claude launch claims (2023) of reliability. A possible baseline, but not one Marcus identified.
Shows math fragility in Oct 2024, but is not matched to any identified promise.
Anthropic's own account of computer use being error-prone while improving. Not tied to any initial promise.

reviews.rationale: The claim names no promiser, date, capabilities or threshold for 'remotely'. The packet confirms there is no identifiable, representative set of promises to compare against. Any verdict would rest on a baseline the speaker did not give, so the claim is too vague to score. The case itself is not broken.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, including his own quoted email to Newton, which he endorses. The 'always say' part is about his own views and is rightly not scored.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' language makes this a scored forecast. The proposition keeps 'not soon' and the need for new ideas. The 'disproven hypothesis' clause is his stated reason, not something to score.

contract.note: The plain reading of AGI as broadly accepted human-level general intelligence is fair. 'Not soon' has no date, so the horizon is open. The scaling versus new-ideas distinction will need judgment later.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The packet found no system broadly accepted as AGI by the evaluation date. The early-contradiction rule (AGI arriving mainly by scaling within a few years) has not been triggered. Nothing can settle the claim as supported until AGI exists, so it stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, stating his view in his own post.

semantics.note: Read in context, the claim means AI is in real everyday use, as his examples show. His personal daily use is rightly left out.

contract.note: The plain reading, AI deployed in widely used consumer products in 2024, is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: Google disclosure, Oct 2024: all seven of its products with 2B+ users, including Maps, use Gemini. This is a company statement about itself, which the contract accepts.
Google disclosure, Oct 2024: AI Overviews in Search reach over 1B users a month.
Pew survey fielded Dec 2022 shows frequent everyday contact with AI. It predates the target period, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: 2024 company disclosures, which the contract accepts as sources, show AI built into search and maps at billion-user scale. That meets the support condition. The packet found no evidence that these products lacked AI. Speech recognition and recommendations were not separately documented, but the core claim does not depend on them.
